basics.name: Sina Mohammadi
basics.label: Ph.D. Candidate, Electrical & Computer Engineering
basics.summary: Ph.D. Candidate in Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of Michigan-Dearborn specializing in Machine Learning for Optimal Power Flow, LLM applications in power grids, distribution network state and topology estimation, and power system protection.

work.name: Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of Michigan-Dearborn
highlights: Proposed two novel methods for topology recovery in low-voltage distribution networks using only smart meter data.
Developed hierarchical clustering of incremental voltage measurements to reveal distribution network topology with high accuracy.
Investigated physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for solving Optimal Power Flow, training a label-free neural network for DC-OPF.

work.name: Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of Michigan-Dearborn
highlights: Courses: ECE 305, ECE 311, ECE 385, ECE 485, ECE 5831.
Taught laboratory sessions for ECE 305 and ECE 311; graded homework, exams, and course projects.

work.name: Department of Electrical Engineering, University of Zanjan
highlights: Proposed a pilot-based unit protection method for meshed microgrids based on apparent resistance estimation of transmission lines.
Evaluated protection scheme efficiency across grid-connected and islanded modes under diverse fault contingencies.

work.name: Department of Electrical Engineering, University of Zanjan
highlights: Led problem-solving sessions on three-phase inductive electric machines and single-phase transformers.
